differential.name: Contrast‑induced acute kidney injury (post‑STEMI PCI)
differential.rationale: Sudden rise in creatinine to 3 mg/dL after recent myocardial infarction suggests nephrotoxic contrast exposure.

differential.name: Acute decompensated heart failure with cardiorenal syndrome
differential.rationale: History of MI, hypertension, obesity and low‑output state can precipitate renal hypoperfusion and rapid creatinine rise.

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease, stage 4 secondary to hypertension/metabolic syndrome
differential.rationale: Long‑standing hypertension, metabolic syndrome and anemia are typical precursors; baseline GFR likely already reduced.

differential.name: Acute tubular necrosis from NSAID overuse for chronic neck/low‑back pain
differential.rationale: Chronic NSAID use can cause intrinsic renal injury, contributing to abrupt creatinine elevation.

differential.name: Acute myocardial infarction (ST‑segment elevation) causing renal hypoperfusion
differential.rationale: Ongoing STEMI can lead to systemic hypotension and prerenal azotemia, worsening renal function.
